# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-6 (Extended v74)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port); **November 17, 1823 (newspaper FALSE ACCOUNT: Jean Valjean drowned; body not found)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern; man in yellow coat rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs, departed with child)**; **December 25-26, 1823 onward (Valjean traveled with Cosette to Dunstead harbor town in England; purchased mourning clothes for Cosette; returned to Paris at nightfall December 26 via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital)**; **1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced; now entering summer of second year of residence)**; **CURRENT TIME: Summer of second year (approximately 1825 or 1826)—present narrative action taking place. CURRENT NIGHT: Valjean actively fleeing with Cosette through le Petit-Picpus district; pursuit imminent**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns); Arras; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Paris (1823-1826) including Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, Jardin des Plantes. **Mouffetard quarter** (Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church). **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as hovel but large internally; first story contains numerous chambers and attics, one occupied by old woman portress; rest uninhabited. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT (Chapter 6, current night)**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, walls and solitude; monkish aspect; roads unpaved, streets unbuilt. **CUL-DE-SAC GENROT**: Exit monitored by Javert's sentinels. **RUE PETIT-PICPUS**: Sentinel positioned, illuminated by full moon. **DROIT-MUR LANE**: Nearly entirely bordered by mean houses on right; on left by solitary severe building with numerous parts growing higher; angle descends to wall forming deeply retreating niche concealed by two corners. **Wall (Rue Polonceau and Rue Droit-Mur)**: Extended from niche angle to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur to gloomy building. **Gloomy building (current refuge location)**: Somber aspect; only one window (two shutters covered sheet zinc, constantly closed); front has ancient cistern pipes of lead with branch patterns resembling old leafless vine-stocks; ancient tree (linden or ivy) above wall; approximately 18 feet height from ground to top of wall; angle formed by wall and gable filled at lower extremity by triangular mass of masonry; niche filled by colossal wretched door (vast formless assemblage of perpendicular planks, upper broader than lower, bound by long transverse iron strips; one carriage gate ordinary dimensions cut roughly 50 years previously). **Discovery**: Door is merely wooden decoration against building; behind planks lies wall of unhewn slabs and blocks of stone. **Weather conditions**: Rain threatened since morning but held off; light went early as season dictated; full moon illuminated streets; frost silvered hedges overnight; wind from water smelling salt and tar.

## Jean Valjean's Current Crisis and Flight (Summer Year 2, Continuing—ACTIVE RESCUE ATTEMPT)
**STATUS**: ACTIVELY FLEEING with Cosette; crisis intensified. **ESCAPE ROUTE (Mouffetard through le Petit-Picpus)**: Traversed labyrinths combining Rue Censier/Rue Copeau, Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor, Rue du Puits l'Ermite; at eleven o'clock from Saint-Étienne-du-Mont traversed Rue de Pontoise in front of commissary police office No. 14; recognized Javert leading four-man pursuit party; slipped under gate, went down Rue des Postes toward Jardin des Plantes; traveled through night with full moon; arrived at le Petit-Picpus district, crossed unsheltered space believing himself out of danger; perceived movement in darkness, recognized Javert and squad. **CURRENT LOCATION (Chapter 6, continuing night)**: Droit-Mur lane in le Petit-Picpus; positioned at wall with gloomy building (ancient cistern pipes and ivy patterns on front); Cosette seated with back against stone post, instructed to be silent. **IMMINENT PERIL**: Seven or eight soldiers in platoon under Javert's command debouched into Rue Polonceau, advancing slowly and cautiously, searching all nooks and embrasures of doors and alleys; advancing toward Valjean's position; at their marching rate with frequent halts, approximately quarter hour to reach him. **DESPERATE REALIZATION**: Few minutes only separate Valjean from "terrible precipice which yawned before him for the third time"; galleys now means not only galleys but Cosette lost forever—life resembling interior of tomb. **ATTEMPTED ESCAPE THROUGH WALL**: Wall approximately 18 feet height; angle with gable has triangular mass of masonry at lower extremity; linden-tree and ivy above wall border garden beyond; Valjean examined for climbing possibility but realized no ladder could be used without moon exposure to watching sentinel; all windows grated with heavy iron bars, even attics; pipe dilapidated and past service. **RESOURCE ACCESSED**: Among numerous prison escapes from Toulon, Valjean is past master in incredible art of climbing walls without ladder or irons, using muscular force alone—leaning on nape, shoulders, hips, knees, using rare stone projections, capable of reaching sixth story; art rendered Conciergerie corner celebrated (Battemolle escape reference, 20 years prior). **COSETTE PROBLEM**: She cannot climb; impossible to carry her (man's full strength required, burden would disturb center of gravity and pull downward). **ROPE SOLUTION**: With supreme energy, Valjean crossed street at bound, entered blind alley, broke latch of lamp-lighter's rope box with knife point, seized rope (street lanterns of Paris descended by rope traversing street side to side, adjusted in post groove, protected by metal case, key kept by lamp-lighter). **ROPE RIGGING (Chapter 6, Excerpt 608)**: Without haste but with firm, curt precision, Valjean undid his cravat, passed it round Cosette's body under armpits (taking care it should not hurt child), fastened cravat to one end of rope using seafaring "swallow knot," took rope's other end in his teeth, pulled off shoes and stockings (threw them over wall), stepped upon triangular mass of masonry, began raising himself in angle of wall and gable with solidity and certainty as though having ladder rungs under feet and elbows. **PROGRESS**: Half minute not elapsed when he was resting on knees on wall.

## Cosette's State (Summer Year 2)
**Age**: Approximately 8.5-9 years old. **Current condition**: Becoming uneasy despite absolute trust in Valjean; plucking his coat skirt anxiously; contented herself with this rather than loud shrieks; unaware specifics of peril but sensing danger from Valjean's absorption and singular gestures; now rigged with cravat fastened by swallow knot to rope, awaiting uplift to wall and safety.

## Javert's Current Status and Pursuit
**ACTIVELY PURSUING**: Formidable officer; commanding platoon of seven or eight soldiers; confirmed leading coordinated search across le Petit-Picpus district; tall figure distinctly visible at head of platoon; advancing slowly and cautiously into Rue Polonceau; searching all nooks of walls, embrasures of doors, alleys; location approaching toward Droit-Mur lane where Valjean positioned; pace deliberate; approximately 15 minutes to reach target position; pursuing with full awareness of district's labyrinthine layout.

## English Community (Harbor Towns: Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Yarlby, Torton, Dunstead, Wilholt)
**Kelford residents**: Volia Brackick (hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; walked long way round avoiding muddy square; fell asleep in chair before fire caught; predicted rain wrongly); Lurald Stenworth (mended torn sleeve by window; married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out, 1824); Nelan (complained of aching back; bought ribbon and regretted it). **Brackick family**: Luwyn Brackick (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Volan Stenworth (son born to Luwyn and Lurald; laughed at story nobody else found funny; stated "price of salt is scandal," agreed by Lurald); Kadrek Brackick (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints; before autumn was out, took Rinelle Corrley in marriage at Kelford, couple lived there thereafter; laughed at story nobody else found funny). **Other locations**: Ostcombe (Wenelle fell asleep in chair before fire caught). **Details from harbor region**: Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; rain threatened since morning but held off; light went early; frost silvered hedges overnight; wind came off water with smell of salt and tar; children chased hoop down lane, shrieking; carts loaded with turnips creaked past well; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; gulls quarreled over heap of fish heads by steps; dog barked at nothing then went quiet; rope and pulley system for street lanterns (rope ascended/descended by means traversing street side to side, adjusted in post groove, pulley fastened underneath lantern, rope protected by metal case, key kept by lamp-lighter).
